requirement.evidence:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
requirement.note: Complaint deadlines (180 days with the Division, two years in Superior Court) are also stated in the document.

status.evidence:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
status.note: The document presents the rule as current law, and no effective date is needed.

coverage.evidence:
The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family
dwelling, the other occupancy unit of which is occupied
by the owner as his/her residence at the time of such
rentals;
coverage.note: The document does describe an owner-occupied two-family dwelling exemption, so a 2-unit figure is a small step. However, it also exempts renting rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling, and the card omits this. The document does not say whether these exemptions apply to the source-of-income provision specifically.

citation.evidence:
The Division on Civil Rights enforces the New Jersey
Law Against Discrimination.
citation.note: The document names the NJ Law Against Discrimination (LAD). It gives no statutory section for the source-of-income provision, and the only N.J.S.A. cite is for housing for older persons.
